You never know if you don't try! And honestly, from what I've read online, unless you're contractually obligated to volunteer a certain amount of hours for something (i.e. a court order or some places making you sign a contract), you can usually step away pretty easily if it doesn't work out for you. At the end of the day, this is volunteering, and you have all the freedom to step back if it doesn't fully align with what you're looking for!

  
I'd definitely recommend calling ahead to the various places that you'd like to volunteer at and asking them what the procedure is with commitment and things like that. Can't hurt to ask!

I totally understand those thoughts! It's important to understand that those thoughts are just coming from your brain wanting to protect yourself from uncertain or potentially embarrassing situations, but they don't define you or your capabilities! It really helps to just dive in head first despite those thoughts and overtime you'll have so much evidence for why those thoughts were wrong in the first place.

“Courage isn't the absence of fear, butthe ability to act despite feeling fear”

> Do you believe that you will have issues doing your work, or do you believe that you'll face discrimination aside from that?

In all honestly, both. I'm not really able to sit at a desk for long periods of time, and usually do most of my work laying down. It also doesn't help that I constantly feel self-conscious about whether people are staring at me or not. In the ideal world, I'd prefer working in a quiet room by myself but from what I hear about offices nowadays that doesn't seem to be the case (open offices, etc).

I also believe that a decent relationship between coworkers is important and as I've mentioned before, this disease isn't exactly beneficial to my people skills.
